540-program-description: Key issues in Indigenous life in Canada: history, art and culture, indigeneity and gender, and resistance.
543-about-the-interdisciplinary-life-sci: Exposure to life sciences; review choices with the adviser. Not for students in Anatomy and Cell Biology, Biochemistry, Honours Immunology, Microbiology and Immunology, Neuroscience, Pharmacology or Physiology.
543-program-description: For earth, physical, math and computing students. 9 credits of basic life sciences, 3 of health and social sciences, 3 of empirical and technological, 9 from any. Same exclusions. Contact the Interdisciplinary Programs Adviser.
544-empirical-science-and-technology: Statistics credit is limited; see Course Overlap. With MATH 324, no credit for GEOG 202, MATH 203, PSYC 204, BIOL 373, MATH 204 or PSYC 305.
612-about-mathematics-and-statistics: One of Canada's oldest departments of its kind, with award-winning researchers. Pure math (algebra, analysis, geometry, number theory, topology), applied math (discrete math, game theory, machine learning, numerical analysis, optimization, probability), and statistics (Bayesian inference, biostatistics, high-dimensional data, survival analysis).
612-undergraduate-program-options: Leads to academia, government, banks, insurance, pharma and high-tech.

Honours in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics and Statistics, including with Physics or Computer Science, are for graduate school and research. Majors are more flexible, leaving room for a minor or second concentration. Statistics can lead to the A.Stat. Also joint majors, a Liberal program, and a B.Com. Major through Desautels.
612-research-opportunities: Funded summer research with faculty, and data analysis through the Statistical Consulting Service.
612-internship-opportunities: Internship Year in Science: 8, 12 or 16 months, usually between U2 and U3. Industrial Practicum: four months from May, 0-credit pass/fail.
612-location: Burnside Hall, Room 1010, 805 Sherbrooke St. W. Contact the Department for advising.
624-about-physics: From subnuclear particles to the universe, with fields that run through all science. Graduates work in industry, government and education.

Honours is demanding, for graduate and professional careers. Three multidisciplinary honours (Math, Chemistry, Computer Science) are even more so. The Major gives broad training with room for other courses.

Enter Honours in first year, or move from the Major after U1 with an adviser's help. Joint majors with Atmospheric Sciences, Computer Science, Geophysics and Physiology. Minors in Electrical Engineering (Physics Major only) and Physics. A biological physics concentration and a Liberal component.
Out-of-province students normally start in Foundation. Prerequisites can sometimes be waived by the professor. B.A. & Sc. has a Major Concentration.
624-internship-year-in-science-iys: Work experience normally between U2 and U3 (p. 1117), available with the Physics Major and Honours, and the joint majors and honours.
624-science-foundation-program: Without a relevant CEGEP program, start with the Foundation Year (p. 1111). With CEGEP Science, start at the 200 level.
624-location: Rutherford Physics Building, Room 108, 3600 University St.
625-program-description: 18 credits, no overlap. No math courses, though many have math prerequisites, so it suits Mathematics students and others with the background. If courses overlap, substitute others after seeing an adviser.
625-program-description-2: B.A. & Sc. or B.Sc./B.Ed. only. Not enough for professional or graduate work in physics; take a B.Sc. for that.
625-required-courses-30-credits: Courses taken elsewhere without credit are replaced from the Complementary list.
634-psychology: See the listed pages for the Department's information.
656-about-sustainability-science-and-soc: Knowledge and skills for moving to a just, sustainable future. Three pillars: Science and Technology, Economics, Policy and Governance, and Ethics, Equity and Justice. Offered by Geography with Bieler.
656-program-description: Improving well-being while protecting Earth's life-support systems, on the same three pillars, run through Geography with Bieler.
Honours adds a supervised research thesis. Program GPA 3.3 to enter, B or higher in ENVR 495, CGPA 3.0 and program GPA 3.3 at graduation. 500-level seminars are encouraged.
657-honours-required-courses: ENVR 495D1 and D2 over consecutive terms, or N1 and N2 otherwise.
657-sustainability-in-business: 3 credits of Management, then 18 from three areas, at least 9 at 300+ and at least 6 from each area.
658-area-3-sustainability-and-biophysica: BIOL 540 or ENVR 540; BREE 217 or GEOG 322, not both of either.
658-program-description: Knowledge and skills for a sustainable future, on the three pillars, with Bieler.
